slides.heading: How Quantum Entanglement Works
slides.body: Einstein called it 'spooky action at a distance' — here's why he was both right and wrong

slides.heading: What Is Quantum Entanglement?
slides.body: When two particles interact in certain ways, they become linked — or entangled. Measuring one particle instantly determines the state of the other, no matter how far apart they are.

slides.heading: Superposition: The Setup
slides.body: Before measurement, a quantum particle exists in multiple states simultaneously — this is called superposition. A photon can be both horizontally and vertically polarized at the same time, until observed.

slides.heading: How Entanglement Is Created
slides.body: Scientists create entangled pairs by shooting photons through special crystals or cooling atoms to near absolute zero. The particles share a quantum state that cannot be described independently of each other.

slides.heading: The Measurement Paradox
slides.body: When you measure one entangled particle, its twin instantly 'knows' the result — even across vast distances. In 2022, researchers confirmed this over 1,200 km using satellite-based experiments.

slides.heading: Why It Doesn't Break Physics
slides.body: Entanglement cannot transmit information faster than light. The result of each measurement is random — you can only compare notes after the fact using classical (slow) communication. No loophole for FTL signals.

slides.heading: Bell's Theorem: Proof It's Real
slides.body: John Bell devised a test in 1964 to distinguish true quantum weirdness from hidden variables. Every experiment since has confirmed: nature is genuinely non-local. The 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics honored this work.

slides.heading: Quantum Computing Applications
slides.body: Entanglement is the core resource in quantum computing. Qubits that share entangled states can process exponentially more information in parallel, powering algorithms that classical computers cannot match.

slides.heading: Quantum Cryptography & Teleportation
slides.body: Entanglement enables quantum key distribution (QKD) — encryption that is physically unbreakable. Quantum teleportation uses entanglement to transfer quantum states (not matter) between locations with perfect fidelity.

slides.heading: The Quantum Future Is Now
slides.body: From unhackable internet to trillion-operation quantum computers, entanglement is transforming technology. The universe is stranger than we imagined — and that strangeness is our greatest engineering tool.
